examples: Cibber, a vamper of other men’s plays, has borrowed from it his favourite Nonjuror, and applied it to the purposes of a political party.
wiktionary.gloss: One who vamps; one who creates or repairs by piecing old things together; a cobbler.

blocks.etymology: From German Wasser (“water”) + Ancient Greek ἔλαιον (élaion, “oil”) + -ine. Genericized trademark of the Vaseline brand of petroleum jelly introduced by American chemist Robert Augustus Chesebrough in 1872.

wiktionary.gloss: Petroleum jelly.
Any particular kind of petroleum jelly or of any similar lubricant.

blocks.etymology: From German Wasser (“water”) + Ancient Greek ἔλαιον (élaion, “oil”) + -ine. Genericized trademark of the Vaseline brand of petroleum jelly introduced by American chemist Robert Augustus Chesebrough in 1872.

examples: Even at this late date, vaselining will preserve the best of these leathers.
wiktionary.gloss: To lubricate with vaseline.

blocks.etymology: From Middle French verification (modern French vérification) or its etymon Medieval Latin vērificātiō. By surface analysis, verificate + -ion.

senses.definition: the act of checking or proving that something is true, accurate, or real

examples.en: The bank sent a text code for identity verification.
examples.vi: Ngân hàng đã gửi mã tin nhắn để xác minh danh tính.

examples.en: We are waiting for official verification of the test results.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đang chờ sự xác minh chính thức về kết quả xét nghiệm.

senses.vi: sự xác minh; sự thẩm tra

thesaurus.definition: additional proof that something that was believed (some fact or hypothesis or theory) is correct
(law) an affidavit attached to a statement confirming the truth of that statement

wiktionary.gloss: The act or process of verifying.
The state of being verified.

examples: The detective needs verification of your whereabouts last night.
wiktionary.gloss: Confirmation; authentication.
A formal phrase used in concluding a plea, to denote confirmation by evidence.
The operation of testing the equation of a problem, to see whether it truly expresses the conditions of the problem.

examples: Whoopee! I won!
wiktionary.gloss: A spontaneous expression of delight or joy.
To behave exuberantly; to make whoopee.

blocks.etymology: An alteration of Middle English hurtilbery, hurtil-beri (see English hurtleberry), analysable as whortle + berry. Compare English huckleberry.

thesaurus.definition: erect European blueberry having solitary flowers and blue-black berries
blue-black berries similar to American blueberries

wiktionary.gloss: Vaccinium myrtillus (bilberry or blue whortleberry);
Vaccinium vitis-idaea (lingonberry or red whortleberry);
Vaccinium uliginosum (bog whortleberry or bilberry).
A berry of one of these shrubs.

blocks.etymology: From wonder + struck.

wiktionary.gloss: Filled or overcome with wonder.

blocks.etymology: From work + shy.

examples: Workshy benefits claimants should stop watching daytime television and get a job.
wiktionary.gloss: Disinclined to work; lazy.
